passages.text: When he had said these things, I replied, “Already I thank God, for just as I wished to be fully assured, so he has also granted it to me. Nevertheless, as far as I am concerned, be so free from worry that I will never doubt—to such an extent that, even if you yourself should ever wish to dislodge me from the prophetic position, being powerless, you will be unable to do so. So firmly do I know what I have received. And do not suppose that you are promising me anything great in this very thing, that I will never doubt. Rather, neither I myself nor any human being who has heard the discourse concerning a prophet will ever be able to doubt the true position, once he has first listened and understood what the truth of prophetic declaration is. Therefore, be confident in the doctrine willed by God, for every artifice of wickedness has been defeated. Against prophecy nothing has any power—neither arts of speech, nor devices of sophistries, nor reasonings, nor any other contrivance—provided, at least, that the person who has listened to a true prophet truly desires truth and is not looking around for something else under a pretext of truth. So, my lord Peter, do not lose heart as though you had bestowed the greatest good on someone insensible; for you bestowed it on someone who recognizes the favor and cannot be led astray from the truth that was given. For I know that it is possible both to receive quickly what one wants and not to obtain it after a long delay. I therefore know better than to despise, because of the speed with which it was given, what was given to me—something incomparable and alone secure.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: to be fully assured
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive denotes being brought to full conviction or assurance, not merely receiving information.

lexical_decisions.chosen: from the prophetic position
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὑπόθεσις can denote a position, thesis, premise, subject, or doctrine; “position” fits something from which Clement might be dislodged while retaining the conceptual ambiguity.

lexical_decisions.chosen: being powerless, you will be unable
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves the source’s emphatic repetition of the cognate ideas rather than smoothing one away.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μήτοι νόμιζέ μοι σὺ μέγα ἐπαγγέλλεσθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: do not suppose that you are promising me anything great
lexical_decisions.rationale: The explicit σὺ is taken as the subject of ἐπαγγέλλεσθαι and μοι as its recipient. Although “do not suppose that I am making a great claim” would fit the broader context, it would reverse the supplied pronouns.

lexical_decisions.chosen: what the truth of prophetic declaration is
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπαγγελία can mean a promise, profession, announcement, or declaration; “declaration” suits the discussion of prophetic discourse without restricting it to prediction of the future.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in the doctrine willed by God
lexical_decisions.rationale: θεοβούλητος describes something intended or willed by God; the dative marks that in which Peter is to have confidence.

lexical_decisions.chosen: devices of sophistries
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπίνοιαι denotes conceptions, inventions, or devices, while σοφίσματα denotes sophistic arguments or sophistries.

lexical_decisions.chosen: as though ... on someone insensible
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀναίσθητος here denotes someone unperceptive or unable to appreciate the gift, not necessarily someone physically unconscious.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μὴ δυναμένῳ ἀπατηθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δοθέντος ἀληθοῦς
lexical_decisions.chosen: cannot be led astray from the truth that was given
lexical_decisions.rationale: The separation expressed by ἀπό supports being deceived or led away from the bestowed true thing; “truth” gives natural English for the substantival neuter ἀληθοῦς.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι ἔνεστιν ὧν βούλεταί τις καὶ ταχέως λαβεῖν καὶ βραδέως μὴ τυχεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: For I know that it is possible both to receive quickly what one wants and not to obtain it after a long delay
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἔνεστιν is taken impersonally as “it is possible,” governing the coordinated infinitives λαβεῖν and μὴ τυχεῖν. The rendering preserves μὴ τυχεῖν as nonattainment and expresses βραδέως idiomatically as “after a long delay.” The positive and negative members present prompt receipt both directly and by contrast with prolonged nonattainment. A less likely alternative takes ἔνεστιν existentially and attaches both infinitives to βούλεταί τις: “there are things one wants both to receive quickly and not to obtain after a delay.” That analysis makes both outcomes objects of desire and gives a less natural relation between ὧν and the two infinitives.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ δοθέντος μοι διὰ τὸ τάχος ἀσυγκρίτου καὶ μόνου ἀσφαλοῦς
lexical_decisions.chosen: because of the speed with which it was given, what was given to me—something incomparable and alone secure
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀσυγκρίτου and μόνου ἀσφαλοῦς agree with the substantival τοῦ δοθέντος, not with τάχος, and describe the gift as incomparable and uniquely secure.

passages.text: When I had said these things, Peter said, “I acknowledge my gratitude to God both for your salvation and for my own delight. For I truly rejoice, knowing that you have recognized what the greatness of prophecy really is. Since, then, as you said, even if I myself should ever wish—which may it never be!—to shift you to a different doctrine, I would not be able to persuade you, begin, from tomorrow onward, to be present with me in the disputations of those who oppose us. Tomorrow is my encounter with Simon the magician.” After saying this and himself partaking of food, he instructed me also to partake separately. After he had pronounced a blessing over the food and given thanks, once satiety had been reached and he had also explained to me the reason for this very thing, he continued, saying, “May God grant you to be made like me in every respect and, once baptized, to share the same table with me.” Having said these things, he instructed me to rest, for by then, I suppose, the body’s nature was also demanding sleep.

lexical_decisions.chosen: I acknowledge my gratitude to God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase expresses thanksgiving while retaining the sense of ὁμολογῶ as acknowledgment rather than replacing it with an unrelated formula.

lexical_decisions.chosen: my own delight
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀπόλαυσις can mean enjoyment, delight, benefit, or fruition; the following ἥδομαι supports the affective sense, though “my own benefit” remains possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: which may it never be!
lexical_decisions.rationale: Literally the wish is that the contemplated event be far away; the English idiom preserves its optative rejection.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in the disputations of those who oppose us
lexical_decisions.rationale: ζητήσεις may be inquiries, discussions, debates, or disputations. The substantival ἀντικείμενοι are opposing persons; “us” makes their contextual opposition explicit without identifying a different object.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἔστι δέ μοι ἡ αὔριον πρὸς Σίμωνα μάγον
lexical_decisions.chosen: Tomorrow is my encounter with Simon the magician
lexical_decisions.rationale: The Greek leaves the event after πρός implicit. “Encounter” preserves the adversarial relation without specifying whether it is formally a debate or contest, and μάγον is translated rather than retained as the Latinized “Magus.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τροφῆς αὐτὸς μεταλαβὼν ἰδία κἀμὲ μεταλαβεῖν ἐκέλευσεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: himself partaking of food, he instructed me also to partake separately
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἰδία is taken adverbially with Clement’s partaking, which is supported by the later explanation about baptism and sharing Peter’s table. It could instead modify Peter’s partaking (“having partaken separately”) or, less likely, the manner of his instruction.

lexical_decisions.chosen: once satiety had been reached
lexical_decisions.rationale: The articular passive infinitive does not state who was satisfied. The impersonal English preserves that ambiguity; “after he had eaten his fill” or “after I had eaten my fill” would choose an unstated subject.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αὐτοῦ τούτου τὸν λόγον μοι ἀποδοὺς
lexical_decisions.chosen: he had also explained to me the reason for this very thing
lexical_decisions.rationale: λόγον ἀποδιδόναι here means to give an account or explanation. The referent of “this very thing” is left open, though the separate partaking is the most immediate contextual explanation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: βαπτισθέντα τῆς αὐτῆς μοι μεταλαβεῖν τραπέζης
lexical_decisions.chosen: once baptized, to share the same table with me
lexical_decisions.rationale: The aorist participle makes baptism antecedent to sharing Peter’s table, while μεταλαβεῖν with the genitive denotes participation or sharing.

lexical_decisions.chosen: for by then, I suppose
lexical_decisions.rationale: που softens the assertion with an inferential “I suppose” or “perhaps,” rather than functioning as a place adverb here.
